subtopics.title: What Globalisation Is — and the Forces That Caused It

questions.question: The lesson's practical test for globalisation is that:
options: Every country uses the same currency
An event on one continent moves prices, jobs and incomes on another within weeks
All trade barriers have been abolished
Each country produces everything it consumes

questions.question: The shipping container transformed world trade because:
options: One uniform box moves from vessel to rail to road without being opened, collapsing freight costs
It doubled the price of ocean freight
It ended the need for ports

questions.question: Production carved into stages, each stationed where it is done best and cheapest, is called:
Which cause belongs to the POLICY family rather than the technology family?
options: Dismantling exchange controls so finance crosses borders freely

questions.question: South Africa's vehicle plants at Kariega, East London and Rosslyn belong on the gains side because:
options: They sell only to South African buyers
Foreign investment built world-scale plants sustaining over one hundred thousand jobs

questions.question: The closure of textile and footwear factories in KwaZulu-Natal and the Western Cape illustrates:
options: The losses side — local industry hollowed out when cheaper imports arrived after tariffs fell

questions.question: The 2008 crisis cost South African jobs because:
options: South African banks had issued the housing loans
The rand was pegged to the dollar
Our customers' economies stopped ordering — contagion through an interconnected system

questions.question: The 'race to the bottom' describes:
options: Mobile multinationals playing governments against each other on tax and standards while rooted workers lose leverage
Countries competing to build the fastest ships

questions.question: The North/South labels are best understood as:
options: Strict geography divided at the equator
Economic shorthand — New Zealand is far south on the map and firmly North in the economy
A voting bloc in the United Nations

questions.question: The terms-of-trade treadmill means an economy that sells raw and buys made:
options: Sets the world price for its exports
Must export more each year merely to afford the same equipment

questions.question: The debt mechanism squeezes Southern budgets when:
options: World interest rates climb or the local currency weakens, swelling foreign-currency repayments

questions.question: Tariffs that stay low on raw cocoa but climb on chocolate historically pushed the South to:
options: Keep shipping its resources unfinished instead of industrialising them

subtopics.title: South Africa Inside the Global Economy

questions.question: South Africa's openness is evidenced by:
options: Exports plus imports amounting to well over half of GDP

questions.question: The African Continental Free Trade Area is the strategic prize because:
options: It removes South African income tax
The continent buys our manufactured goods — vehicles, machinery, processed food — not only our ores
It fixes the rand to the dollar

questions.question: 'South Africa contains the whole divide within its own borders' means:
options: Our northern provinces are richer than the southern ones
We trade only with Northern countries
Northern-grade finance around the Johannesburg exchange coexists with Southern-style raw-export dependence
We have left all trade blocs

questions.question: The two-handed policy debate weighs deeper integration against:
options: Strategic protection — tariffs and local-content requirements while industries rebuild

questions.question: Reading a phone 'like a passport' reveals:
options: It was made entirely in one factory
At least six countries folded into one object — design, chip, screen, minerals, assembly, cable

questions.question: Door one — 'it had to become possible' — was opened by:
options: Containers making goods cheap to move and cables making information instant

questions.question: South Africa's own door two swung open when:
options: The world's shops and investors returned after 1994
The first container port was built

subtopics.title: One Shop Now — Who Won and Who Lost on Our Streets

questions.question: Cheap imports work like 'a pay rise nobody announces' because:
options: Tariff revenue is paid to workers
The same wage buys more when world-shop prices are lower

questions.question: The silent footwear works of Pietermaritzburg show that trade's losses land on:
options: Whoever competes head-to-head with the world's cheapest producer

questions.question: 'One shop, one flu' summarises how:
options: A foreign financial collapse in 2008 cut South African shifts and around a million jobs within the downturn

questions.question: The economist's answer to 'is globalisation good or bad?' is that it:
options: Grows the total and moves the shares — so policy must spread gains and cushion losses

subtopics.title: Top of the Map, Bottom of the Map

questions.question: In the chocolate bar story, Ghana keeps a sliver while Europe keeps the rest because:
options: The finishing — roasting, branding, retail — is where the money lives, and it happens up north
Chocolate cannot be made in Africa

questions.question: The three weights on the southern side of the map are:
options: Raw-for-made trade, dollar-denominated debt, and weak voice where the rules are written

questions.question: Africa's continental free trade area answers the divide by aiming to:
options: Ban all imports from the North permanently
Keep the finishing — and the profit — inside Africa by letting Africa sell made goods to Africa

questions.question: Which development is redrawing the North/South map?
options: China and India dragging the world's economic centre southward while BRICS demands a Southern seat
The end of all Southern debt
